igbo: Onye wetara oji wetara ndụ
english: He who brings kola nut brings life
meaning: Hospitality and generosity are the foundations of community. The kola nut is not merely food — it is the act of welcome itself.

igbo: Egbe bere, ugo bere; nke si ibe ya ebena nku kwaa ya
english: Let the kite perch, let the eagle perch; whichever says the other should not, let its wing break
meaning: Live and let live. Peaceful coexistence is not weakness — it is the condition for everyone's survival.

igbo: Onye aghana nwanne ya
english: Do not abandon your sibling
meaning: Family and community loyalty run deeper than personal convenience.

igbo: Otu onye tuo izu, o gbue ochu
english: If one person plans alone, they fail
meaning: Important decisions require counsel. Community thinking is stronger than individual cleverness.

igbo: Onye kwe, chi ya ekwe
english: When a person agrees, their personal spirit agrees also
meaning: Your destiny responds to your determination. What you commit to with your whole self, the universe conspires to support.

igbo: Aka nri kwọọ aka ekpe, aka ekpe kwọọ aka nri
english: The right hand washes the left, the left hand washes the right
meaning: Mutual support is the only kind that truly works. We clean and sustain each other.

igbo: Ọ bụ mfe ilu ogwe osisi, ma ọ dịghị mfe ilu ndụ
english: It is easy to cut a stick but not easy to live a life
meaning: Life's challenges cannot be resolved with quick shortcuts. Patient endurance is what makes a whole life.

igbo: Mmadụ bụ ihe kachasị mma n'uwa
english: A person is the most precious thing in the world
meaning: Human life and relationship are the ultimate currency. No achievement or wealth outweighs the value of another human being.

igbo: Eze dị n'ime ọnụ
english: The king is in the mouth
meaning: Words have power. What you say shapes your reality and your relationships. Speak with care.

igbo: Ajụjụ adịghị eme mmadụ ihere
english: Asking questions does not embarrass a person
meaning: Curiosity is a sign of intelligence. The one who asks learns; the one who pretends to know stays ignorant.

igbo: Ndụ bụ ụzọ, ọ bụghị ọnọdụ
english: Life is a journey, not a destination
meaning: The value of living is in the movement, the relationships, the learning — not in arriving at any fixed point.

igbo: Chukwu gozie aka ya n'olu
english: God blesses the hand in its labour
meaning: Divine favour meets human effort. Do your part faithfully and leave the rest to something larger than yourself.

igbo: Osisi na-ada n'akụkụ ka ọ dara
english: A tree falls toward where it leans
meaning: Your habits and daily choices shape where you end up. You become what you consistently move toward.

igbo: Ụzọ bụ n'anya, ma ọ bụghị n'ụkwụ
english: The road is in the eye, not in the foot
meaning: Vision and intention come before movement. Know where you are going before you take a step.

igbo: Ụlọ dị mma mana o nweghị mmadụ
english: A house may be fine but without people it is nothing
meaning: Wealth and property mean nothing without love and community. The people in your life are the true furnishing of a home.

igbo: Ihe di mma n'ọnụ adịghị mma n'afọ
english: What is sweet in the mouth may not be sweet in the stomach
meaning: Be wary of things that seem attractive but may have hidden costs. First impressions are not the whole truth.

igbo: Ihe mmadụ si n'obi ya pụta ka mma
english: What comes from the heart speaks better
meaning: Authentic expression — even if imperfect — carries more weight than polished insincerity.

igbo: Nke ọma abịa, nke ọjọọ gbaa ọsọ
english: Let good things come, let bad things run
meaning: A hopeful disposition is a choice. Orient yourself toward the good, and the bad has less to hold onto.

igbo: Ihe mmadụ ji eme ihe bụ obi ya
english: What drives a person is their heart
meaning: Character determines action. Look to the inner life to understand why people do what they do.

igbo: Onye nwere obi ọma adịghị enyo obi ọjọọ
english: A person with a good heart does not wear a bad one
meaning: What is inside cannot stay hidden for long. Goodness and its opposite both reveal themselves through time.

igbo: Ọ bụ ihe e ji n'aka nọrọ ya
english: What is in the hand stays in the hand
meaning: Take care of what you have. Stewardship of present gifts is the qualification for greater ones.

igbo: Chi onye adịghị ura n'oge ya na-aga ije
english: One's chi does not sleep while they are on a journey
meaning: Your personal spirit watches over you especially when you are vulnerable or far from home.

igbo: Onye wetara mmanya wetara udo
english: He who brings wine brings peace
meaning: Generosity dissolves tension. The person willing to give freely is the one who can heal rifts that words alone cannot.

igbo: Nwata kọọ ihe okenye pụọ ọsọ, ọ dịghị mma
english: It is not good for a child to say what makes an elder flee
meaning: Wisdom deserves respect. The young should speak with care, especially before those who have lived more.

igbo: Aka nri kwọọ aka ekpe
english: The right hand washes the left
meaning: No one succeeds entirely alone. Support flows both ways in every healthy relationship.

igbo: Onye nwere isi agwaghị ya ka ọ dee n'ala
english: A person with a head is never told to use it as a pillow
meaning: Natural intelligence and gifts should be used, not wasted. What you were born with was not given to be left unused.

igbo: Ihe ọjị eme na-eme n'oge ya
english: What kola nut does, it does in its own time
meaning: Patience is not passive — it is faith in correct timing. The right moment for things cannot be rushed.

igbo: Ọ bụ n'afọ ya ka ọ na-eji ọrụ ya
english: It is from the belly that one pushes their work
meaning: Motivation comes from genuine need and drive. Know what you are working for and carry that knowledge inside you.

igbo: Nwa mgbeke na-agụ ife n'oge mmiri ozuzo
english: The lazy child reads when the rain comes
meaning: Some people only make effort when they have no other choice. Diligence should not require crisis to summon it.

igbo: Ihe onye metara ya adịghị egbu ya
english: What one has done to another does not kill the doer immediately
meaning: Consequences for wrongdoing may be delayed, but they are never cancelled. Act as though justice is always watching.

igbo: Nwoke bụ agụ, nwanyị bụ mmiri
english: The man is a leopard, the woman is water
meaning: Different strengths complement each other. Force and flexibility, boldness and endurance — a partnership needs both.

igbo: Ọ bụrụ na ị maghị ebe mmiri bidoro maba gị, ị gaghị ama ebe ọ kwụsịrị
english: If you do not know where the rain began to beat you, you cannot know where it stopped
meaning: Understand your origins and your history. You cannot chart where you are going without knowing where you came from.

igbo: Egbe bere, ugo bere
english: May the kite perch and may the eagle perch
meaning: The essence of justice and coexistence — everyone deserves their place. Deny another's right to be, and you forfeit your own.

igbo: A na-eji nwayọ eri ihe dị ọkụ
english: It is with patience that one eats a hot meal
meaning: Difficult or delicate matters require calm and care. Rush a hot thing and you only burn yourself.

igbo: Otu mkpịsị aka rụta mmanụ, ọ zụọ ọ zụrụ ndị ọzọ
english: When one finger touches oil, it spreads to the others
meaning: One person's actions — good or bad — affect the whole family or community. We are bound together; no one falls or rises entirely alone.

igbo: Ọ bụ mgbe ọ kụ na-akụ ka a na-akụ ya
english: The iron is struck while it is hot
meaning: Act when the moment is ripe. Opportunity has a season; seize it before it cools.

igbo: Nwata bunie nna ya elu, akpụkpọ ya ọ mịnye ya
english: If a child lifts his father up, his own clothing covers the father's nakedness
meaning: When the young support the old, the honour returns to the family. Caring for your elders is caring for your own name.

igbo: Onye ji onye n'ala ji onwe ya
english: He who holds another down holds himself down too
meaning: Oppressing or hindering others traps you as much as them. You cannot keep someone in the ditch without staying in it yourself.

igbo: Agwọ emeghị nke o ji bụrụ agwọ, umuaka achacha ya
english: A snake that fails to show it is a snake will be tied up by children as firewood
meaning: Command appropriate respect through your conduct. Fail to show your worth and even the small will take you for granted.

igbo: Ọ bụghị ụbọchị niile ka eji eri anụ
english: It is not every day one eats meat
meaning: Good times and abundance are not constant. Appreciate the feast days, and prepare wisely for the lean ones.

igbo: Ebe onye dara ka chi ya kwaturu ya
english: Where a person falls is where their chi pushed them down
meaning: There is meaning even in our stumbles. A setback may be redirecting you; where you fall can teach you where to rise.

igbo: Mmiri riri enyi, ọ dịghị agba mmiri
english: The water that swallowed the elephant does not overflow with pride
meaning: True power does not boast. The genuinely great absorb even the mighty without making noise about it.

igbo: Onye maara ihe ọ na-eme, ọ na-eme ya nwayọ
english: One who knows what they are doing does it gently
meaning: Mastery brings calm. Panic and haste betray the amateur; the skilled work without commotion.

igbo: Nkịta si na ihe ya ji achị ọsọ bụ nʼihi na ọ maghị ihe na-eso ya
english: The dog runs because it does not know what pursues it
meaning: Fear born of ignorance drives frantic action. Understand the real situation before you flee from shadows.

igbo: Ọ bụ nwayọọ nwayọọ ka e ji aracha ọka dị ọkụ
english: It is gently, gently that one licks hot corn
meaning: Approach difficult or sensitive matters with patience and care; force only causes harm.

igbo: Onye lụọ ọgụ nna ya, ọ na-elu ya na mgbagbu
english: Whoever inherits their father's quarrel inherits its wounds
meaning: Be careful which conflicts you take on. Old grudges carried forward bring old injuries with them.

igbo: Maka na ọ dịghị mma, ka anyị jiri gaa nwayọ
english: Because the road is not good, let us go slowly
meaning: When circumstances are hard, prudence and patience matter more than speed. Adapt your pace to the terrain.

igbo: Ọ bụ ofu mkpụrụ ọka ka e ji mara ọka ọ chara acha
english: It is by a single grain that one tests whether the corn is ripe
meaning: A small sample reveals the whole. Judge wisely from telling details rather than demanding the entire harvest first.

igbo: Onye na-agba ọsọ na onye na-achụ ya nwere otu ebe ha na-eje
english: The one fleeing and the one pursuing are headed the same way
meaning: Adversaries are often more bound together than they realise. Conflict links two fates on a single road.

igbo: Ukwu na-eje ije na-ebute akụ
english: The feet that keep walking bring home wealth
meaning: Persistence and effort, not luck, gather prosperity. Keep moving; the road rewards the traveller who does not stop.

igbo: Onye nwụrụ n'oge ọkọchị anaghị echefu ya n'udu mmiri
english: One who suffered in the dry season does not forget it in the rains
meaning: Hardship endured teaches lessons that comfort should not erase. Remember the lean times even when times are good.

igbo: Nwaanyị mụta ọgụ mgba, ọ na-agba ya n'ụlọ di ya
english: When a woman learns to wrestle, she wrestles in her husband's house
meaning: Skills and habits, once formed, express themselves at home. Cultivate the character you actually want to live with.

igbo: Aka aja aja na-ebute ọnụ mmanụ mmanụ
english: Soil-covered hands bring an oil-filled mouth
meaning: Honest, dirty work leads to a well-fed life. There is no clean shortcut around effort.

igbo: Ọ bụ n'ọnụ ka mmadụ ji ama ezi okwu
english: It is by the mouth that one is known for truth
meaning: Your reputation is built word by word. Consistent honest speech is what earns you a trusted name.

igbo: Onye buru ibu ọ ga-ata ahụhụ
english: He who carries a heavy load will feel its weight
meaning: Every responsibility has its cost. Take on what you can bear, and be ready to endure the burden you accept.
